ahrf_rural_urban_code.short_description: USDA rural-urban continuum code classifying counties from metro to rural (1–9).
ahrf_rural_urban_code.long_description: USDA Economic Research Service Rural-Urban Continuum Code. Codes 1–3 are metropolitan counties (by population size of metro area); codes 4–9 are nonmetropolitan counties ranging from urbanized adjacent to metro areas (4) to completely rural or less than 2,500 urban population not adjacent to a metro area (9). The AHRF technical documentation lists this variable with 2013 vintage codes, so check the vintage before using it for trends.
ahrf_rural_urban_code.statement: In {location}, the rural-urban continuum code is {value}.

ahrf_pcp.long_name: Non-Federal Primary Care Physicians in Patient Care (Excluding Residents)
ahrf_pcp.short_description: Count of non-federal primary care physicians (MDs and DOs) in patient care roles, excluding hospital residents.
ahrf_pcp.long_description: Number of non-federal primary care physicians (including both MDs and DOs) actively in patient care, excluding hospital residents and those age 75 or older. Primary care includes general practice, family medicine, general internal medicine, general pediatrics, and obstetrics/gynecology. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
ahrf_pcp.statement: In {location}, there are {value} primary care physicians in patient care.

ahrf_md_all.long_name: Non-Federal Medical Doctors in Total Patient Care
ahrf_md_all.short_description: Count of non-federal MDs across all specialties in patient care roles.
ahrf_md_all.long_description: Total number of non-federal medical doctors (MDs) in patient care roles across all specialties. Includes office-based, hospital-based, and other patient care settings. Does not include federal physicians or DOs. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.
ahrf_md_all.statement: In {location}, there are {value} MDs in patient care.

ahrf_psych.long_description: Total number of non-federal psychiatrists (MDs), across all activity categories (patient care, administration, teaching, research). AHRF reports child and adolescent psychiatrists as a separate variable, which this pipeline does not pull. Source: AMA Physician Masterfile compiled by HRSA.

ahrf_dentists.long_name: Dentists with Active National Provider Identifier
ahrf_dentists.short_description: Count of dentists with an active NPI in the county.
ahrf_dentists.long_description: Number of dentists with an active National Provider Identifier (NPI) in the county, derived from the CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES). Includes all dental specialties.
ahrf_dentists.statement: In {location}, there are {value} dentists with an active NPI.

ahrf_hospitals.short_description: Total number of hospitals in the county.
ahrf_hospitals.long_description: Total count of hospitals in the county across all types (short-term general, specialty, long-term, psychiatric, rehabilitation, and other). Source: American Hospital Association (AHA) Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.

ahrf_critical_access_hosp.short_description: Number of Medicare-certified critical access hospitals in the county.
ahrf_critical_access_hosp.long_description: Count of hospitals certified as Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) by CMS. CAHs are rural hospitals with 25 or fewer acute care inpatient beds, located more than 35 miles from another hospital, that receive enhanced Medicare reimbursement to maintain access to care in rural areas. Source: AHA Annual Survey compiled by HRSA.
ahrf_critical_access_hosp.statement: In {location}, there are {value} critical access hospitals.

ahrf_population.long_description: Total county resident population, from the Local Area Personal Income (LAPI) estimates that HRSA carries in AHRF as the 'Population (Persons)' variable. The AHRF also includes separate Census County Population Estimates, which this pipeline does not pull.
ahrf_population.statement: In {location}, the estimated total population is {value}.

ahrf_good_air_pct.long_name: Percentage of Days with Good Air Quality
ahrf_good_air_pct.short_description: Percentage of measured days rated 'Good' by EPA Air Quality Index.
ahrf_good_air_pct.long_description: Percentage of measured days in the county rated 'Good' (AQI 0-50) on the EPA Air Quality Index report, as carried in AHRF. Counties with no air quality monitoring data have no value.

ahrf_pm25.long_name: Annual Average Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Concentration

ahrf_pm25.long_description: Annual average ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration in micrograms per cubic meter, from the CDC Environmental Public Health Tracking Network as carried in AHRF. In the 2025 release, values exist only for 2019 and 2020. Counties without monitoring stations may have NA values.

ahrf_pop_density.short_description: County population density per square mile from Census data.

ahrf_medicare_per_capita.long_name: Actual Medicare Fee-for-Service Per Capita Expenditure

ahrf_medicare_per_capita.long_description: Actual (not price-standardized) Medicare fee-for-service per capita expenditures for county residents enrolled in traditional Medicare. ahrf.name: Area Health Resource File (AHRF)
ahrf.description: The Area Health Resource File (AHRF) is an annual county-level database produced by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA). It aggregates data from over 50 sources including the AMA Physician Masterfile, the American Hospital Association Annual Survey, the Bureau of Health Workforce, CMS Medicare claims, the Census Bureau, and EPA air quality monitoring. The AHRF covers all U.S. counties and territories with measures of health workforce supply, health facility counts, demographics, socioeconomic conditions, health expenditures, and environmental factors. It is widely used in health services research to characterize county-level resource availability and identify shortage areas.
ahrf.restrictions: Public domain. HRSA data is produced by a U.S. federal agency and is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

_catalog.summary: The AHRF compiles county-level measures of health workforce supply, hospital and facility counts, shortage-area designations, Medicare utilization and spending, demographic and environmental conditions, and maternal and infant health (births, infant deaths, low birth weight, and obstetric and neonatal hospital capacity) from over 50 federal sources.
